## This week

One chapter, two halves of one subject. A finished output can be fed back into the attempt so the next version is better — reflection (Self-Refine on one output, Reflexion across attempts, and the external-feedback condition that decides when self-correction works at all) — or scored against a fixed standard so change itself becomes measurable — evaluation (evalsets, code grading, LLM-as-a-judge and its biases, error analysis, regression). The lecture also draws the line students most often blur: ReAct's Thought versus reflection.

## Lab

`W5_lab_reflection_evals.ipynb` — the two halves run as one experiment: draft → critique → revise on an essay, then the claim "V2 beats V1" put through a five-criterion binary judge over a fixed set, error analysis, and prompt iteration against a numeric target. Adapted from Andrew Ng's *Agentic AI* Modules 2 and 4.

Homework: `W5_hw_chart_reflection.ipynb` — the reflection loop where the output is a rendered matplotlib chart and the critique reads the image itself. Due before Week 6.

Run it in Colab: click **Open in Colab** (links above), paste your API key into the setup cell ([API Setup](api-setup.qmd)), and run top to bottom.
